subject: english-literature
source_note: Topic structure follows the Edexcel A-Level English Literature (9ET0) specification. Connections, sequence and prerequisites are expert-authored teaching relationships (exam boards do not publish these).

units.name: Component 1: Drama
units.blurb: Shakespeare plus one other drama, tragedy or comedy

units.name: Component 2: Prose
units.blurb: Two thematically linked prose texts, comparative

units.name: Component 3: Poetry
units.blurb: Post-2000 anthology with unseen poetry, plus specified poetry

units.name: Coursework (NEA)
units.blurb: Independent comparative study of two chosen texts

topics.name: Shakespeare
topics.blurb: One set Shakespeare play, tragedy or comedy

topics.name: Critical Anthology
topics.blurb: Critical essays on tragedy or comedy supporting the Shakespeare study

topics.name: Other Drama: Tragedy
topics.blurb: A second tragedy from the set list

topics.name: Other Drama: Comedy
topics.blurb: A second comedy from the set list

topics.name: Childhood
topics.blurb: Comparative prose pair on the theme of childhood

topics.name: Colonisation & its Aftermath
topics.blurb: Comparative prose on empire and its legacy

topics.name: Crime & Detection
topics.blurb: Comparative prose on crime and detection

topics.name: Science & Society
topics.blurb: Comparative prose on science and its social impact

topics.name: Women & Society
topics.blurb: Comparative prose on women's place in society

topics.name: Poems of the Decade & Unseen
topics.blurb: Post-2000 anthology compared with an unseen poem

topics.name: Specified Poetry: Metaphysical
topics.blurb: The Metaphysical Poets or John Donne

topics.name: Comparative Coursework Essay
topics.blurb: Independent comparison of two freely chosen texts

connections.why: The critical anthology supplies the theory of tragedy or comedy applied to Shakespeare
Critical concepts of tragedy frame the reading of the second tragic drama
Critical concepts of comedy frame the reading of the second comic drama
Both develop close analysis of dramatic genre, structure and character
Comparing Shakespeare with another comedy sharpens genre understanding
Tragic downfall and transgression connect drama to the crime-and-detection theme
Both themes foreground domestic life and social roles, inviting comparison
Both explore the unknown and humanity's limits, one rational and one uncanny
Both examine power, voice and marginalisation in society
Comparative reading of theme and voice transfers from prose pairs to paired poems
Reading modern poetry against the Romantics highlights changing form and context
Tracing poetic movements shows how ideas of love, nature and faith evolve
The Victorians respond to and revise Romantic themes and forms
Modernism breaks from Victorian convention, best seen by comparison
The Movement reacts against Modernist excess, a contrast worth tracing
Thematic prose comparison is the core skill the independent NEA demands
Comparative poetry analysis feeds the wide reading required for the NEA
Studying drama supplies texts and critical approaches for the coursework comparison
